title: Isabella by John Everett Millais
episode: The first Pre-Raphaelite painting by Sir John Everett Millais
description: The first painting Millais showed as a Pre-Raphaelite, in 1849, based on a Keats poem: a family dinner where one brother kicks a dog and glares at his sister’s suitor. It is in the Walker Art Gallery.

title: Spring (Apple Blossoms) by John Everett Millais
episode: "full of beauty and without subject," Sir John Everett Millais,  Spring (Apple Blossoms)
place: Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight
description: A row of young women picnicking under apple blossoms, with a scythe at the edge of the picture. It is in the Lady Lever Art Gallery, built by the soap maker William Lever across the Mersey at Port Sunlight.

title: The Beguiling of Merlin by Edward Burne-Jones
episode: Edward Burne-Jones, The Beguiling of Merlin
place: Lady Lever Art Gallery, Port Sunlight
description: Burne-Jones’s painting of the enchantress Nimue trapping the wizard Merlin in a hawthorn tree with his own spell, first shown in 1877. It hangs in the Lady Lever Art Gallery at Port Sunlight.
